Exercise E.S21 — Hard: A product bound can miss useful structure
      
        For $f(x)=\operatorname{ReLU}(x)-\operatorname{ReLU}(-x)$, write its two-layer weights without biases. Compute the product of their spectral norms and the exact global Lipschitz constant. For binary classification by the sign of $f$, compare the certified radii at $x=2$.
        Review if needed: this section and gradients and the chain rule.
        
          Show hint
          Check separately $x\ge0$ and $x\lt0$. The network represents a familiar scalar map.
        
        
          Show worked solution
          The first-layer column is $W_1=(1,-1)^\top$ and the second-layer row is $W_2=(1,-1)$. Each has spectral norm $\sqrt2$, so the product bound is $2$.For either sign of $x$, $\operatorname{ReLU}(x)-\operatorname{ReLU}(-x)=x$. Its exact global Lipschitz constant is $1$.At $x=2$, the margin is $2$. The product bound certifies every radius below $2/2=1$, whereas the exact constant certifies every radius below $2$. The boundary is at zero, distance $2$; equality would permit a tie.
